business: Zlatara Opal — a small goldsmith/jeweller on Zlatarska ulica (Miljana Vukova 2, Podgorica) that makes one-off pieces in 14k gold and 925 silver to a customer's drawing; no catalogue, no stock, no prices, orders happen by Instagram DM or in the shop.
artDirection: A warm ivory jeweller's-counter page: paper-coloured grounds, hairline champagne rules, and photography treated as objects laid out on cloth rather than as product tiles. The reference is a small atelier's own printed card and display case — a museum-label voice under every photograph, a mat-board frame around the map, nothing glossy or "luxury-brand" theatrical. Restraint is the whole art direction: two typefaces, three grounds, one cool accent, one moving element per interaction, and every claim on the page traceable to something the shop actually does (`data.ts` header explicitly forbids inventing prices, stock or hours).
signatureElements: Museum/case-label captions under every photograph (page.tsx figcaption in the hero and in each gallery figure): a Newsreader serif title on one line, then the material spec in 0.68rem uppercase / 0.3em tracking — "Ogrlica sa motivom sirene / ZLATO 14K (585)". This is exactly how a jeweller labels a piece in a vitrine, and it is the single element that carries the brand across hero, gallery and phone.

The hand-set gallery rail: `PIECE_LAYOUT` in page.tsx maps every photo src to its own column span (4/5/3, then 5/3/4 on a 12-col grid) AND its own aspect box (square, 3/2, 5/6, 4/3, 4/5, 6/5). No two frames share a width or a crop, so the six photos read as six separate shoots — which is literally true — instead of a matched product grid. The record is typed `Record<(typeof pieces)[number]["src"], …>` so adding a piece to data.ts is a compile error until it gets a deliberate layout.

Hero photograph bleeding off the text rail on one side only (`lg:col-span-7 lg:-mr-8 xl:-mr-16`): the image runs past the container to the right while the type block stays inside it. The page is built off-centre from the first screen, without any decorative asymmetry.

Champagne hairline rules that draw themselves left-to-right (`.rule` + `opal-draw`, scaleX 0→1 on `animation-timeline: view()`): the divider above each collection and each process step arrives as a drawn line rather than sitting there as a border. One idea, used twice, in place of scattered fade-ins.

The italic reserved as a scarce resource: Newsreader is loaded with a real drawn italic (the page.tsx font comment says that is the only reason italics exist here), and it appears in exactly three places — the hero kicker sentence "Zlato i srebro, po narudžbi", and two words inside two headlines ("tvoju priču", "crteža"). It reads like handwriting on a card, not like a style.

The mat/passe-partout map frame: `border border-[--opal-line] p-1.5` around the MapEmbed, so the map sits inside a display mount instead of being a full-bleed grey rectangle. The map itself stays unloaded behind a real button drawn as a graphed plate.

A dark graphite contact rail fixed to the bottom on phones (md:hidden, 1.2fr/0.8fr), showing the actual Instagram handle @zlataraopal next to a Pozovi cell — the counter of the shop, weighted to the channel this business really uses.
typography: Two families only. Newsreader (subsets latin+latin-ext, normal + true italic) as display; DM Sans as the quiet interface/body face. Hierarchy comes from FAMILY SWITCH + SIZE + COLOR, almost never from weight — the only bold on the page is `font-medium` on buttons and nav. Scale is fluid and deliberately unequal per section: h1 `clamp(2.5rem,7.5vw,4.25rem)` at leading 1.02 / tracking -0.015em; most h2 at `clamp(1.8rem,4vw,2.6rem)`; but the "Od crteža do komada" process heading gets the page's widest type, `clamp(2rem,5vw,3.25rem)`, because the commissioning conversation is the actual product (the code comments say so). Sub-levels: serif 2xl for collection terms, serif lg for gallery titles, serif 4xl champagne-deep numerals for the three steps, serif 2xl for the phone number so the contact detail is display type, not body text. One caps register only — a single shared `eyebrow` constant (0.68rem, uppercase, 0.3em tracking) used for nav, material specs and section kickers, so caps never drift. Body copy is DM Sans in muted grey at `leading-relaxed`, capped by `max-w-xs/md/xl` so no measure ever runs long. Nothing is centred except button labels.
color: Seven scoped tokens in opal.module.css, each annotated with its measured contrast: ivory #f7f2ea (page ground), shell #efe7db (process band), graphite #26221f (text and the two dark surfaces — primary button, mobile rail), muted #6a625a (5.4:1 body), champagne #b89a64 (2.4:1 — explicitly restricted to rules, borders and large display letterforms), champagne-deep #7e6029 (5.2:1 — every small word set in the accent), blue #b9c6d8 (+ blue-deep). The important move is the two-tier accent: the shop's colour is too pale for text, so the pale mix carries lines and big glyphs and a deep mix of the same hue carries anything small — the brand colour survives without an accessibility compromise. Grounds create rhythm rather than decoration: ivory → ivory → shell → ivory → blue/25 → ivory → ivory, with hairline `--opal-line` borders only where two same-coloured sections meet. The opal blue appears exactly once as a surface (the gift band at 25%) — one cool note in an entirely warm page.
composition: Hero (page.tsx §1): 5/7 split on a 12-col grid, text left, photograph right bleeding -mr-8/-mr-16 past the rail. `lg:items-center` so the type block sits optically centred against a much taller image. On mobile the order flips (`order-1`/`order-2`) so the page opens on the object, not on a headline.

Collections (#kolekcije): 4/8 split — a short heading occupies a whole third of the width and does nothing else, and the four categories live in a 2×2 `<dl>` on the right. Using a description list (dt/dd) instead of four cards is why this section has no card chrome at all: just a drawn rule, a term, a definition.

Process (#narudzba): the only full-width tinted band, and the only section that starts flush-left with a caps kicker + the page's largest heading. Three `<ol>` columns, each opening with a graphite hairline and a large champagne numeral, then a closing paragraph at `max-w-xl` that undercuts the whole thing: "Nema korpe ni naručivanja preko sajta."

Gallery (#radovi): a section header split baseline-aligned — heading bottom-left, a short right-aligned note at `sm:items-end` — then the 12-column ragged rail. Because spans and crops differ, the caption baselines deliberately stagger down the row; the ivory between frames does the framing, there are no cards.

Gift band: two columns aligned to their BOTTOM edge (`lg:items-end`), heading left, paragraph right — a quiet interlude between the gallery and contact, distinguished only by the blue ground and the two hairline borders.

Contact (#kontakt): 50/50. Left is an `<address>` set as typography — street as an h2, city, phone as 2xl serif link, handle with a ↗ — spaced on a 5/7/8 rhythm rather than a table. Right is the matted map plate, which is the same visual weight as a framed photograph.
Footer: a single flex row, wordmark + the honest disclaimer ("Nezvanični dizajn koncept…") pinned bottom-aligned against the VibeLab credit.
interaction: Photo settle (`.settle`, opal-settle 1.06→1 on `animation-timeline: view()`, range entry 5% → cover 45%): gallery images come to rest as they enter. Earns its place — it reads as a camera finding the piece, and it is the only motion on the images. Guarded by `@supports` + `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`, so it is pure progressive enhancement (Chromium only; other browsers get the static page, which is fine).

Rule draw (`.rule`, scaleX 0→1, transform-origin left): the hairlines above collections and steps draw in. Same mechanism, second job. Because both effects are scroll-timeline CSS with no JS and no per-child delays, this avoids the banned 'scattered scroll-reveal' pattern — nothing fades, nothing translates, nothing staggers.

Grow-from-left underline (`.underline`, background-size 0→100% 1px, 0.4s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)) on the phone number and the Instagram handle only. Explicitly called 'the page's only interactive flourish' in the CSS. It fires on `:focus-visible` too, so keyboard users get the same feedback.
Buttons change colour, never position: primary graphite → champagne-deep on hover; the header CTA inverts to graphite fill. No lift, no shadow, no scale.

Secondary CTA breaks the studio's usual outline-inverts-on-hover recipe (documented in the page.tsx comment): a soft champagne fill from the start, deepening on hover, so the two hero buttons read as a pair rather than as primary + ghost.
The map is inert until asked: MapEmbed renders a drawn grid plate plus a real <button>, and only mounts Google's iframe on click — a privacy and performance decision surfaced as a design element.
Focus is one shared constant (`focus-visible:outline-2 outline-offset-4` in champagne-deep) applied to every interactive element, including the sticky bar (with inset offset so it isn't clipped).
mobile: At 390px the page reorders rather than shrinking. The hero photograph moves above the type (order-1/order-2) so the first thing on screen is a piece of jewellery with its case label; the h1 floors at 2.5rem and still breaks over two lines cleanly. The 2×2 collections `<dl>` and the three-column `<ol>` collapse to single columns, and their hairline rules go full width, which turns them into a rhythm of drawn lines down the page — the structure survives because it was never card-based. The gallery loses its 12-col spans (they only apply at lg) but KEEPS the per-photo aspect boxes, so the single column still has square, 3/2, 5/6, 4/3, 4/5 and 6/5 frames in sequence: the "no matched set" idea is carried by crop instead of by width, which is the cleverest part of the responsive design. The desktop header CTA hides below sm and is replaced by the fixed graphite bottom rail (min-h-16 cells, weighted 1.2fr Instagram / 0.8fr phone, `pb-[env(safe-area-inset-bottom)]`), with the body reserving `calc(5rem + safe-area)` of bottom padding so nothing is ever covered. Section padding steps from py-16 to py-24 at sm, so mobile is tighter without losing the ground-colour rhythm. Weak spot: below md there is no in-page navigation at all — the four anchors simply vanish.

transferableIdeas.idea: Per-item hand-set layout map, type-locked to the content
transferableIdeas.why: The `PIECE_LAYOUT` record in page.tsx gives every photograph its own column span and aspect ratio, so a gallery cannot degenerate into a uniform card grid — and because it is keyed by content id (`Record<(typeof pieces)[number]["src"], …>`) rather than by array index, adding an item is a TypeScript error until someone makes a real layout decision about it. It makes 'designed, not generated' structurally enforced.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: For any business with a set of real objects or projects — a bakery's breads, a garage's restorations, an architect's builds — define spans + crops per item in one typed map next to the grid. Choose ratios so items in a row land within ~50px of each other in height (the file comments on exactly this) so the rag looks intentional, not broken.

transferableIdeas.idea: Caption the photo the way the business physically labels the thing
transferableIdeas.why: "Ogrlica sa motivom sirene / ZLATO 14K (585)" is a vitrine label, and it does three jobs at once: it identifies, it proves domain knowledge, and it gives the page a repeatable typographic motif (serif line + tracked caps line) that needs zero decoration.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: Find the business's real labelling convention and set it as a two-line caption pattern: bakery = name + flour/fermentation, garage = model + year + work done, contractor = site + m² + material, restaurant = dish + origin of the ingredient. Never invent the second line; if the fact isn't known, drop the line rather than fake it.

transferableIdeas.idea: Two-tier accent colour (pale for rules and big glyphs, deep for small text)
transferableIdeas.why: opal.module.css splits the brand champagne into #b89a64 (2.4:1, explicitly rules-and-display-only) and #7e6029 (5.2:1, everything small). A pale brand colour usually forces either an accessibility failure or abandoning the colour; this keeps both. Each token carries its measured ratio in a comment, so nobody misuses it later.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: Take any client colour that is too light or too saturated for body text, mix a darker sibling of the same hue, and write the rule into the token comments: pale = borders, rules, oversized letterforms, tints; deep = any word under ~24px. Works for pastel, neon and metallic brands alike.

transferableIdeas.idea: Ground-colour rhythm instead of section decoration
transferableIdeas.why: Three grounds (ivory / shell / blue-25%) sequenced ivory-ivory-shell-ivory-blue-ivory give the page its pacing, and hairline borders appear only where two same-coloured sections abut. No dividers, no wave shapes, no gradients — yet every section boundary is legible.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: Pick two tinted siblings of the page ground and assign each to the ONE section it means something for (here: the process band and the gift band). Never alternate mechanically; the tint should mark a change of subject, and the cool/warm break should happen at most once.

transferableIdeas.idea: Scroll-driven CSS with `animation-timeline: view()` — two effects, one job each
transferableIdeas.why: `opal-settle` (image 1.06→1) and `opal-draw` (rule scaleX 0→1) are pure CSS, no JS, no observer, no per-child delay chains. Wrapped in `@supports` + `prefers-reduced-motion`, they are free where supported and invisible where not. Constraining the page to two motions with clear meanings avoids the scattered-reveal slop pattern entirely.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: Budget exactly two scroll motions per page and give each a stated reason. Good generic pairs: image settle + rule draw; number count-in + underline draw; caption rise on the hero image only. Always ship under `@supports (animation-timeline: view())` so it is enhancement, never a dependency.

transferableIdeas.idea: Break the container on one side, once
transferableIdeas.why: `lg:col-span-7 lg:-mr-8 xl:-mr-16` on the hero figure makes the page read as off-centre from the first screen. It costs one utility class and does more for 'this was art-directed' than any amount of ornament, because the eye registers a broken rail immediately.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: Choose one image per page — usually the hero, occasionally a mid-page full-bleed — and let it overhang the container on the side away from the type. Do it exactly once; a second overhang cancels the first and just looks like a container bug.

transferableIdeas.idea: Contact block set as display typography, not as an info table
transferableIdeas.why: In #kontakt the street becomes an h2, the phone number is a 2xl serif link with a growing underline, the city is a single line, and the tap targets are min-h-11. The section is the page's second-most typographic moment, which is correct: for a shop with no checkout, the address IS the conversion.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: Wherever the real conversion is a call or a visit, promote the phone/address to heading scale, use `<address>` semantics, and give the number the page's one hover flourish. Then say the honest operational caveat in small muted type underneath instead of padding it with icons.

transferableIdeas.idea: Let the absence of data be copy
transferableIdeas.why: "Radno vrijeme nije navedeno jer se javni izvori razlikuju — prije dolaska najkraće je pozvati" and "Nema korpe ni naručivanja preko sajta" turn two missing features into trust and into a call to action. It is also why the layout never needed a fake stat row or a fake catalogue to fill space.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: List what the business genuinely doesn't have (prices, hours, online ordering, stock) and write one plain sentence per gap that redirects to the real channel. Place it as the closing line of the section that would otherwise have contained the missing feature.

transferableIdeas.idea: Mobile action rail shaped to the business's real channel, not a generic 'Call now'
transferableIdeas.why: The sticky bar is weighted 1.2fr/0.8fr toward Instagram because this shop takes orders by DM, and it prints the actual handle rather than a label — the visitor can act on it even after leaving the page. It is a dark graphite band, which is the only place the page goes dark, so it reads as the shop counter.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: Decide which channel actually converts for this business, give it the larger cell and show the real identifier (handle, number, Viber), and set the whole rail in the page's darkest token with safe-area padding plus matching body bottom padding. Two cells maximum.

transferableIdeas.idea: Deliberately break your own component recipe once, and note why
transferableIdeas.why: The secondary CTA drops the studio's usual outline-inverts pattern for a soft champagne fill, with a comment explaining that it makes the two hero buttons read as a pair. Reused engineering, non-reused visual identity — exactly what stops a set of demos from looking like one template.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: On every new page, pick one shared recipe (button pair, caption style, section header, list marker) and re-solve it for this brand, then leave a one-line comment saying what the brand argument was. The comment is what keeps the next pass from 'fixing' it back to the default.

weaknesses: The 'Poklon koji ostaje' blue band is the weakest section on desktop — at 1440px it is a wide pale strip holding one short heading and one paragraph, with a large empty middle. It reads as a spacer rather than a section. If you transfer the one-cool-band idea, give that band real content (a photo, a date, a specific occasion) or fold it into the gallery intro.

The three-step process section is very close to the house-banned 'decorative 01/02/03 numbering' idiom, and the four-item collections block is close to 'hairline-border list'. They survive here because the steps are genuinely sequential and the list is a real `<dl>` with no chrome — but these two sections are the most portable and therefore the most dangerous parts of the page. Do not carry them to a business where the content isn't actually a numbered sequence or a set of definitions.

The gallery's staggered caption baselines are intentional but sit right at the edge of reading as misalignment: in the desktop shot the three captions in row 1 land at three noticeably different heights, and the tallest gap leaves a visible column of empty ivory. On a page with less confident photography this would just look broken.

Below md there is no navigation at all — the four section anchors are simply hidden and nothing replaces them. Acceptable for a short one-page concept, not transferable to any page with more sections or with content people need to jump between.

The secondary hero button's border is champagne (#b89a64) on ivory, roughly 2.4:1 — the label text is fine, but the button's own edge is barely visible, so at a glance the hero can look like one button plus a tinted text block. Use the deeper mix for the border if you reuse the pattern.

The `clamp(1.8rem,4vw,2.6rem) leading-[1.1] tracking-tight` heading recipe is retyped inline four times, and `eyebrow`/`serif`/`focus` are ad-hoc string constants at module scope. Fine at one page, but this is copy-paste styling that will drift; a section-heading component or a CSS class is the right shape once a second page needs it.

All motion depends on `animation-timeline: view()`, which is Chromium-only — Safari and Firefox visitors see a completely static page. That is the correct tradeoff here, but don't present the settle/draw as 'the design' when most of the interaction budget is invisible to a large share of visitors.

The tablet breakpoint gets the least attention: at 768px the gallery falls back to a plain 2-up (`sm:grid-cols-2`) and the 12-column rail — the section's signature — disappears entirely, leaving a fairly ordinary two-column grid with ragged bottoms.
